quarterly_data.signal: Q3 2026 results (CEO Haviv Ilan, CFO Julie Knecht): revenue $6.1 billion, up 11% sequentially and 28% year over year, with growth across all end markets and regions; Analog grew 32% and Embedded Processing 21% year over year, Other declined 6%. Industrial grew more than 40% year over year (about 10% sequentially), automotive mid-teens (about 10% sequentially), data center about 95% (about 20% sequentially; about 13% of revenue), personal electronics about flat year over year (upper single digits sequentially), communications equipment grew. Gross profit $3.9 billion, 64% of revenue, up 280 basis points sequentially (higher revenue, plus some pricing, loadings and mix); operating expenses $1 billion; operating profit $2.9 billion, 47% of revenue, up 73%; net income $2.4 billion or $2.62 per share. Cash flow from operations $3.4 billion; capex $463 million in the quarter; trailing 12-month free cash flow $8.4 billion (up from $2.4 billion), including $1.6 billion of CHIPS Act incentives (investment tax credit and direct funding). Inventory $4.7 billion (+$67 million), 194 days.
quarterly_data.figure: Q3 revenue $6.1 billion (+28% YoY); data center about +95% YoY; operating margin 47%; EPS $2.62

quarterly_data.signal: Outlook (CFO Julie Knecht, CEO Haviv Ilan): Q4 2026 revenue $5.8 billion-$6.3 billion and EPS $2.45-$2.79; effective tax rate about 13% in Q4 and about 13%-14% for 2027; Q4 opex flat to slightly up; long-term model of 75%-85% fall-through excluding depreciation. CEO: data center, industrial and automotive drive the above-seasonal Q4 guide. 2026 capex expected between $2 billion and $3 billion, 'maybe on the higher end' if tool deliveries arrive as planned (tool lead times are extending, especially back-end); 2027 capex color comes on the February capital management call, as a function of the growth TI wants to support. Pricing: after flat pricing in the first half of 2026, TI saw 'a little bit of an uptick' in the second half, mainly in Analog, and is now in 2027 pricing discussions tied to the supply customers want guaranteed, to be reported in January.
quarterly_data.figure: Q4 revenue $5.8 billion-$6.3 billion; Q4 EPS $2.45-$2.79; 2026 capex $2 billion-$3 billion

quarterly_data.signal: Capacity and supply (CEO Haviv Ilan, IR head Mike Beckman): demand is broadening and lead times 'may be ticked a little bit higher', but the CEO says TI remains 'the most competitive supplier in terms of lead time'; outside China little Analog capacity has been added in the four years since the COVID peak, and some Analog supply has gone offline as foundries move to non-Analog parts, so the supply-demand mismatch is higher in Analog. TI has the clean room, sub-fab and long-lead equipment slots reserved for 2027 and beyond and will modulate tool installations to demand; Lehi 1 still has plenty of clean room and the Lehi 2 shell is in the last stages of completion; the Silicon Labs acquisition adds another clean room to move foundry-made parts into Lehi. TI is 'not getting as much as we wanted from our OSAT partners', and its new Malaysia assembly and test site, its largest, is ramping quickly. Some industrial and data center customers asked for help and TI could supply from inventory and commit capacity into 2027 and beyond; automotive customers held little inventory and are struggling to ramp.

End-market views (CEO Haviv Ilan, Mike Beckman): TI sells about 10,000 different generic part numbers into the data center market, growing every quarter (telemetry, cooling, power density), with application-specific sockets in early ramps on 300mm; Beckman: more power, more power density and higher voltages each mean more opportunity for TI; the CEO sees no data center slowdown. Industrial reached its Q3 2022 level, its first new peak in four years, with more content per system; strong sectors include aerospace and defense, energy infrastructure and test and measurement (the latter two closely tied to data centers) and robotics, where TI's content per humanoid is 'somewhere between $500 to $1,000' and 2027 should bring 'a great deal of ramps'. Automotive: the hybrid electric and powertrain sector grew about twice as fast as automotive overall, driven by China and the U.S., including Chinese EV exports. Embedded Processing gross margin has been improving 'a couple of points per quarter', about 10 points year over year 'or something', per the CEO.
quarterly_data.figure: about 10,000 part numbers sold into data center; $500 to $1,000 TI content per humanoid
